problem.statement_latex: For security parameter $\lambda$, fix the folded Reed--Solomon code $C_\lambda\subseteq\Sigma^n$ from Lemma 4.2, where $n=\Theta(\lambda)$ and $|\Sigma|=2^{\lambda^{\Theta(1)}}$. Given oracle access to $H:\Sigma\to\{0,1\}^n$, output $c\in C_\lambda$ satisfying $H_i(c_i)=1$ for every coordinate $i$. This NP search relation has a publicly checkable witness. Complexity uses random-oracle queries and gates; $H_i$ denotes output bit $i$.

quantum.headline_latex: $\operatorname{poly}(\lambda)$ gates and at most $n\lambda$ quantum queries, by Yamakawa--Zhandry, with success $1-\operatorname{negl}(\lambda)$ over random $H$. Prepare the code superposition and coordinate states supported on $H_i^{-1}(1)$, Fourier transform both, coherently add and decode the dual code, then inverse transform. Verification uses $n$ classical hash queries and polynomial code-membership work. A salted two-message construction handles nonuniform provers.

classical.headline_latex: For fixed $0<c<c'<1$ in the code construction, every computationally unbounded classical algorithm using at most $2^{\lambda^c}$ oracle queries succeeds with probability at most $2^{-\Omega(\lambda)}$ (Lemma 6.9). Random codeword trials provide an $O(n2^n)$-query exponential comparator on typical random oracles. The keyless bound concerns uniform algorithms; the keyed construction treats oracle-dependent advice. Substituting an explicit cryptographic hash makes hardness an assumption about that family.
